pedagogy.rationale: Learners build numbers with a paper place-value chart before reading and writing them in words and expanded form.

objectives.statement: Read and write whole numbers up to hundred thousand
objectives.subject: MATH

assumptions: Learners can read and write numbers to 10,000 (Grade 3).
Learners know the digits 0-9 and the ones, tens and hundreds places.

misconceptions.description: Leaves out the zero in an empty place, writing 8,304 for eighty thousand, three hundred four.
misconceptions.response: Build the number in the chart: an empty column still needs a 0 so the other digits stay in their places.

misconceptions.description: Gives the digit instead of its value, saying the 4 in 47,305 is worth 4.
misconceptions.response: Ask which place the digit sits in, then read the value of that place: 4 ten thousands is 40,000.

scenes.title: A big number at the county office
scenes.learnerAction: Read the number aloud with a partner.

content.body:
Mr. Kollie works at a county education office. His list says the county's schools have **47,305** learners (an illustrative number, not a real statistic).

How do you read a number that big? Today you will find out what each digit is worth.

accessibility.textAlternative: A county office lists 47,305 learners. The lesson asks how to read a number that large.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Read the text, then press Tab to reach Continue.

offline.note: Text only; works from the saved lesson.

scenes.title: What you will be able to do

content.body: By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
keyPoints: Name the place and value of each digit in a number up to 100,000.
Read and write numbers up to 100,000 in words, numerals and expanded form.

accessibility.textAlternative: Goal: name the place and value of each digit, and read and write numbers to 100,000.

scenes.title: Every digit has a place
scenes.learnerAction: Read and say the place names in order.

content.body:
From the right, the places are **ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands** and **hundred thousands**.

The place tells the value of a digit. In 47,305 the 4 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 40,000. The 0 is in the tens place: there are no tens, but the 0 must stay so the 3 keeps its hundreds place.
keyPoints: Each place is worth ten times the place to its right.

accessibility.textAlternative: Places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 47,305 the 4 is worth 40,000 and the 0 holds the empty tens place.

scenes.title: Build 47,305 one place at a time
scenes.learnerAction: Open each step to build the number and its expanded form.

content.body: Open each step. Watch how each digit's value adds up to the whole number.

steps.label: 0 in the tens place
steps.description: No tens. The 0 holds the place.

steps.label: 5 in the ones place
steps.description: 5 ones = 5. Expanded form: 40,000 + 7,000 + 300 + 5 = 47,305, read forty-seven thousand, three hundred five.

hints: Start from the left: the biggest place first.

accessibility.textAlternative: 47,305 is 4 ten thousands (40,000), 7 thousands (7,000), 3 hundreds (300), 0 tens and 5 ones: 40,000 + 7,000 + 300 + 5.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Each step is a button; press Enter or Space to open it in order.

scenes.title: Build numbers in the place-value chart
scenes.learnerAction: Place digit cards in the chart for numbers your teacher calls.

content.body: Use your paper place-value chart and digit cards. Build each number your teacher calls, then read it aloud to your partner.

interaction.prompt: Drag each digit card into its place in the chart to build 62,418.

fallback.content: Draw a place-value chart (hundred thousands to ones) in your book. Write 6, 2, 4, 1 and 8 in the right columns for 62,418, then read the number aloud and write it in words.

scenes.expectedObservation: Learners place 6 in ten thousands, 2 in thousands, 4 in hundreds, 1 in tens, 8 in ones and read sixty-two thousand, four hundred eighteen.
hints: Count the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands.

accessibility.textAlternative: Build 62,418 in a place-value chart: 6 ten thousands, 2 thousands, 4 hundreds, 1 ten, 8 ones.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Use the paper chart; on screen read the instructions and press Continue.
accessibility.nonPointerAlternative: Write each digit in the correct column of a drawn chart instead of dragging.

offline.note: The paper chart and digit cards are the core modality; no device needed.

scenes.title: Quick check
scenes.learnerAction: Choose an answer for each question.

content.body: Choose an answer for each question. You will see feedback straight away.

items.prompt: What is the value of the 6 in 36,152?

options.feedback: That is the digit. Which place is it in? Thousands, so it is worth 6,000.
Count the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands. The 6 is in the thousands place.
Yes. The 6 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 6,000.
The 3 is in the ten thousands place. The 6 is one place to the right.

items.prompt: Which numeral is eighty thousand, three hundred four?

options.feedback: This is missing a zero. Build it in the chart: the thousands place is empty and needs a 0.
Yes. 8 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 3 hundreds, 0 tens, 4 ones.
Three hundred four has no tens: the 4 belongs in the ones place.
That is eight hundred thousand. Eighty thousand has only five digits.

hints: Build the number in your chart first.

accessibility.textAlternative: Two questions: the value of 6 in 36,152, and the numeral for eighty thousand, three hundred four.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to each option and press Space to choose; feedback is read aloud.

scenes.title: Write numbers three ways
scenes.learnerAction: Write each number in words and in expanded form.

content.body: Write each answer in your own words and numbers.

hints: Read the number in two groups: the thousands, then the rest.

accessibility.textAlternative: Write 62,418 in words and 90,372 in expanded form, using the text boxes.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to each text box and type; Continue when both are written.

offline.note: Answers are kept on this device.

content.body: Answer each question. Your answers are checked by the school's learning system, not on this device.

fallback.content: Your teacher gives the same questions on paper and records your answers.

accessibility.textAlternative: Final questions on place value, read and answered with the keyboard or touch.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to each option and press Space.

offline.note: Answers wait on the device and are scored after reconnecting.
